aliases: China Jinping Underground Laboratory Phase II

coordinates.locator: Position walked along the OSM Jinping traffic-tunnel line by the sourced portal-to-hall distance (see geometry:cjpl-ii-point method)
coordinates.note: The position is derived along an OpenStreetMap trace of the Jinping traffic tunnel from the distance to the CJPL-II halls published in an arXiv paper. Neither is a surveyed hall position, so the point is shown as campus-grade and approximate. It replaces an earlier geocoder point of 2.5 km precision (28.1763431, 101.720304).

depth.locator: Sec. 1, arXiv:2511.11050; Table I of arXiv:1801.00587 gives CJPL-II 2,400 m
depth.note: Rock cover of CJPL as a whole; the sources give no hall-specific thickness for CJPL-II. This replaces an earlier 2100 m credited to the 2014 second-phase paper (arXiv:1404.2651), which says CJPL-II halls lie under overburdens of about 2.4 km of rock.
depth.quote: is shielded by approximately 2,400 m of vertical rock coverage

depth_mwe.note: No CJPL-II-specific water-equivalent depth is published. The CJPL-wide average of about 2400 m of vertical rock at 2.8 g/cm^3 gives the 6720 m.w.e. that Wu et al. (2013) published for CJPL-I; the 2025 CJPL-II paper states about 2,400 m of vertical rock. This replaces an earlier "~2100 m.w.e.", which the cited 2014 paper does not state. (The quoted "g/m 3" is the paper's own typo for g/cm^3.)
depth_mwe.quote: corresponds to the water equivalent depth of 6,720 m (assuming a rock density of 2.8 g/m 3)

muon_flux.note: Hall C2 of CJPL-II, plastic-scintillator muon telescope, 161 muons in 1098 live days (October 2016 to December 2020); the efficiency was obtained by simulating underground muon energies and angles and the telescope response. The efficiency-uncorrected flux is (1.70 ± 0.13) × 10^-10 cm^-2 s^-1. The paper calls the result the lowest among underground laboratories worldwide. The quote's factor 10^-10 multiplies the whole bracket, so the stored value is 3.03 × 10^-10 cm^-2 s^-1 with no unit conversion.
muon_flux.quote: The cosmic-ray muon flux is determined to be (3.03 ± 0.24 (stat) ± 0.18 (sys)) × 10−10 cm−2 s−1

name: CJPL-II
notes: The completion date for CJPL-II civil engineering (reported elsewhere as December 2023) was not confirmed on an official page and is therefore not recorded as a sourced interval on the facility.

summary.plain: A newer, larger extension of the Jinping underground laboratory, about half a kilometre from the original hall along the same tunnel, also under more than two kilometres of rock.
summary.technical: CJPL-II: a second-phase extension of CJPL, ~500 m west of CJPL-I along the same traffic tunnel, with four planned caverns (14 m × 14 m × 130 m each) and ~2400 m of vertical rock overburden (~6720 m.w.e.); civil engineering credited elsewhere to Tsinghua University and Yalong River Hydropower Development Company (not confirmed on an official page).
